Sign a PDF in your browser

Open the PDF, draw or type your signature, click where it goes and download the signed file. The document is processed only in this browser tab and never uploaded.

How to sign a PDF

  1. Select Open PDF and choose the document.
  2. Select Sign, then draw your signature or type your name.
  3. Click the page where the signature goes. Drag it to move it, and set its width in the panel.
  4. Select Download to save the signed PDF.

How your files are handled

Your files are opened, changed and saved by this browser tab. Nothing is uploaded, and the original file on your device is never modified. Closing the tab discards everything, so download your result first.

Questions

Are my files uploaded?
No. Everything runs in your browser with PDF.js and pdf-lib. Your documents are never sent to a server.
Is this a digital signature?
No. It places an image of your drawn or typed signature on the page. It is not a certificate-based digital signature, so it adds no cryptographic proof of who signed and does not detect later changes.
Can I add the date or my printed name?
Yes. Select Add text and click where the date or name should go.
Is it free?
Yes. There is no account, no watermark, no daily limit and no paid tier.
What are the limits?
Up to 50 MB per PDF, 100 MB in total and 200 pages. Password-protected PDFs are not supported.
